The Nifty 50 closed at 23,053.1, up 0.51% for the day, while the broader Nifty 500 slipped 0.21%. Advance‑decline data showed 401 advances versus 378 declines, giving a weak breadth score of 28.9. Only 27.9% of stocks were above their 20‑day moving average, indicating limited participation. Bank Nifty fell 0.41% to 54,686.95, with its 200‑day average still far above at 56,711.79, suggesting the index remains under pressure.

Foreign Institutional Investors (FII) added INR 3,114.68 crore, extending a four‑day buying streak, while Domestic Institutional Investors (DII) sold INR 392.2 crore, marking two consecutive days of outflows. The FII‑FII futures net long position is modest at 10.6%, and net contracts are negative (‑233,199). Sector strength was seen in IT, pharma, healthcare, PSU banks and infrastructure, whereas media, private banks and financial services weakened. Options data show a put‑call ratio (PCR) of 1.67 for Nifty, indicating more put interest, with max‑pain at 23,250 and resistance (call wall) near 24,000.

Watch the 23,032.77 support (S1) and 23,145.77 resistance (R1) on Nifty, plus the 23,293‑23,589 expected range. A break below the 23,000 put wall could trigger further selling, while a hold above the 23,250 max‑pain level may allow the index to test the 23,400‑23,500 zone. Keep an eye on global cues such as falling Brent crude (‑11.4%) and US market weakness, which could influence risk appetite in the next session.
